lines.text: A person clicks save. The interface says it worked. Seconds later, an agent operation finishes and silently erases their change.
WebMCP makes websites callable. Interleave makes those human-and-agent moments testable—before they become data loss.
This is a source-verified reproduction of Plane issue ninety-six seventy-four, pinned to public code. Nine native WebMCP tools. Zero live systems touched.
The agent queues Plane’s metadata crawler. While it waits, a person saves “Human verified runbook.” The delayed worker returns—and replaces it with “Plane documentation.”
Interleave records the exact interleaving: native dispatch, manual edit, native overwrite. Then it names the rule, and shows expected versus actual.
The same recording replays deterministically. Four reduction attempts collapse the failure to three commands: start crawl, edit metadata, release.

Against current Plane, the test fails. Against the proposed compare-and-set, the stale worker is blocked and human intent survives. Export the regression. Export the five-file patch. Thirteen new cases. Thirty-seven out of thirty-seven Plane tests passing.
Interleave is a reusable concurrency assurance layer for agent-callable applications. Record the race. Prove the failure. Ship the fix.
